title: Multiple Equivalent Simultaneous Offers
description: Present two or three packages of equal value at once, and learn what they really want.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Instead of one offer, you present several that are worth roughly the same to you but differ in shape. Their choice reveals their priorities without a direct question.

sections.title: Why It Works
sections.content: Comparing options forces the other side to reveal preferences. Because the packages are equivalent to you, whichever they pick, you are no worse off — and you learn what to trade.

sections.title: Real-Life Examples
content: Offering a higher fee with a longer timeline, or a lower fee paid sooner.
Offering extra support in one package and a discount in another.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: Two or three clearly distinct packages presented together.
Options designed to be equal in value to the person offering them.

sections.title: How to Use It
sections.content: Build options that differ on dimensions you care little about and they may care a lot about. Present them as a set and watch which one they reach for.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: Options engineered so that one is obviously designed to be refused.
Complex packages that hide the real cost.

sections.title: Defense Strategies
content: Ask what each option is worth to them and to you.
Do not assume the package you like best is the best value.

sections.title: Mistakes People Make
content: Building options that are not actually equivalent.

sections.title: Key Lessons
content: Several equal offers teach you what matters.
Design options you can live with either way.
